title: Quantization cost experiments log (SCM v1 calibration) — measured vs estimated deltas
body:
Purpose
- Track quantization profile experiments used to calibrate SCM v1 cost attribution.
- Compare measured $/1K output tokens vs SCM estimate deltas relative to fp16/bf16 baseline.
- Record anomalies by model family + likely root cause.
- Feed follow-ups into quant profile metadata (expected compute/memory deltas, constraints) and SCM confidence heuristics.

Scope / non-goals
- Not a quality report (we record 1–2 high level quality signals only to flag “unacceptable” configs).
- Not billing (SCM remains technical cost estimate + attribution; do not use numbers for invoice/customer pricing).

Definitions / setup notes
- Baseline is fp16 (or bf16 when fp16 unavailable) on same region + GPU SKU.
- “Measured cost” derived from metered runtime telemetry + infra cost tables (internal), normalized to $/1K output tokens.
- “SCM estimate” is cost-model-service estimate endpoint using request + runtime signals where available.
- Unless called out, tests are decode-heavy prompts (~1K prefill, ~1K decode) to stress KV + decode kernel behavior.
- All tests run with same admission control settings; post-18618 fix for batch_size_effective is required for comparability.

Columns
- profile_id: quant profile identifier used by runtime + catalog.
- quant_type: weight-only int8/int4, smoothquant, fp8, etc.
- mem_delta_expected: from profile metadata (what SCM assumes); mem_delta_measured: from GPU memory telemetry.
- compute_delta_expected: from profile metadata; compute_delta_measured: from tokens/sec deltas at fixed concurrency.
- scm_delta_%: SCM’s predicted % change in $/1K vs baseline.
- measured_delta_%: measured % change in $/1K vs baseline.
- gap_pp: measured_delta_% - scm_delta_% (percentage points).
- confidence: SCM confidence output (high/med/low) captured at time of run.

Experiment log (latest at top)

Quick readouts (what seems stable)
- Llama family: int8 weight-only and int4 AWQ are generally predictable; SCM gaps usually within ~0–5pp when runtime signals are present.
- Qwen2: int8 weight-only looks fine; int4 GPTQ shows recurring underperformance vs SCM assumptions (esp decode).
- Gemma: strong anomalies for int4 AWQ on L40S (throughput drop + cost increase) -> likely kernel path / quant calibration mismatch.
- Mixtral (MoE): int4 AWQ seems risky; compute overhead from dequant + gating dominates at our tested concurrency.

Anomalies / hypotheses (needs follow-up)
1) Gemma-2-27B on L40S + int4 AWQ (QCE-034)
- Observed: measured cost +3% (worse), SCM predicted -20% (better). Gap +23pp, confidence low.
- Hypotheses:
  - Quant profile metadata assumes dequant kernels available; actual path falls back to less optimized kernels on L40S.
  - Activation outliers / calibration: effective compute increases (more stalls) even though weights smaller.
  - Batch efficiency degraded due to longer per-request decode time -> fewer effective batches.
- Action: require “supported_skus” + “known_slow_paths” fields in quant profile metadata, surfaced to SCM assumptions.

2) Mixtral-8x7B MoE + int4 AWQ (QCE-037)
- Observed: throughput -4%, p95 latency +22%, measured savings only -6% vs predicted -21%.
- Hypotheses:
  - MoE routing introduces additional ops not scaled down with weight-only quant.
  - Dequant overhead per expert cancels benefits; cache behavior differs.
- Action: treat MoE family as separate “model_family_cost_behavior=moe”; add family override coefficients for AWQ.

3) Qwen2 + int4 GPTQ (QCE-040)
- Observed: SCM says -18%, measured -9% (gap +9pp), confidence low.
- Hypotheses:
  - Profile compute_delta_expected too optimistic for qwen2; kernel selection not matching expectations.
  - KV cache interactions: slightly worse cache hit behavior -> higher decode compute.
- Action: update compute_delta_expected per model_family OR encode “expected_compute_delta_by_family” (but watch metadata bloat).

SCM-specific notes (inputs/signals that materially change estimate)
- batch_size_effective: pre-18618 bug caused optimistic costs in high concurrency runs; do not compare runs before 2025-02-07 unless re-run.
- prefill_vs_decode split: quant benefits are stronger on decode-heavy; if split missing SCM assumes default 35/65 prefill/decode which can be wrong.
- kv_cache_hit_rate: warm cache runs reduce decode compute; SCM needs accurate hit rate to avoid overstating savings.

Quality smoke signals used (very rough)
- “pass”: no obvious regressions on small prompt set (internal eval harness), no obvious formatting issues.
- “warn”: minor degradations (e.g., more truncations / repetition) but not conclusively attributable.
- “fail”: unacceptable; do not recommend.
Notes: We saw “warn” coincident with the gemma + AWQ anomaly, but not enough evidence to blame quality. Keep separate from cost.

Follow-up tasks (as of 2025-03-04)
- [Arjun] Quant profile metadata updates
  - Add supported_skus list and/or “not_supported_skus” for profiles that regress (initially: gemma + L40S + awq int4 v3).
  - Add model_family_overrides for compute_delta_expected where consistent (candidate: qwen2 + gptq int4).
  - Clarify baseline precision field (fp16 vs bf16) and how SCM should map when baseline differs.

- [Mateo / Omar] Runtime profiling for anomalies
  - Gemma + L40S: confirm which kernel path is used for awq int4 v3; identify fallback.
  - Mixtral MoE: break down dequant overhead across experts; see if batching policy hurts.

- [Logan / Nadia] Telemetry
  - Ensure mem_delta_measured uses consistent definition (peak allocated vs reserved). Current mix is causing confusion when comparing runs.
  - Confirm kv_cache_hit_rate tags not missing in rolling restarts (saw some “unknown” in early Feb).

- [Jordan] SCM calibration / confidence
  - Confidence should drop when profile_id is unknown OR signals missing OR model_family_override absent (today it mostly drops only on missing signals).
  - Add explicit assumption text when model_family_override is applied (“family coefficient: moe_awq_v1”).

Open questions
- How far do we go with model-family specific overrides before we lose “standard” in SCM?
  - Proposal: allow small set of well-justified family coefficients with strong audit trail + versioned profile metadata.
- Do we need to model quantization’s impact on cache hit rate (indirect)? Right now SCM treats hit rate as input only.

Appendix: command / harness notes (informal)
- Harness: internal perf-canary runner with fixed prompt set; one run = 200 requests after 50 request warmup.
- Cost normalization: $/1K output tokens using metered GPU time * internal SKU cost rate; excludes network + storage.
- For reproducibility: always record commit hash of runtime + cost-model-service next time (missing in older runs). Next edit: add columns runtime_sha, scm_sha.
